labels.text: Burkina Faso requests French forces to withdraw from its territory after suspending a military accord that allowed the presence of French troops in the country.

The second round of the 2023 French Polynesian legislative election is held; the Tāvini Huiraʻatira party wins a majority of seats. Moetai Brotherson, Tāvini Huiraʻatira's deputy leader, is elected President of French Polynesia.
Danish cyclist Jonas Vingegaard wins the Tour de France for the second consecutive time.
The 2023 Rugby World Cup is held in France and is won by South Africa who beat New Zealand in the final at the Stade de France, claiming a record fourth Rugby World Cup title.
2023 Nigerien crisis: French President Emmanuel Macron announces that France will end its military presence in Niger and will recall its ambassador from the country.

2024 French legislative election: The left-wing New Popular Front wins the most seats in the National Assembly, upsetting a first-round victory by the far-right National Rally, but fails to achieve a majority.
The 2024 Summer Olympics are held in Paris, France. The controversial opening ceremony and the boxing match of Luca Hámori and Imane Khelif spark international debate.
The 2024 Summer Paralympics are held in Paris, France.
2024 French political crisis: Michel Barnier becomes the first prime minister of France to lose a motion of no-confidence since Georges Pompidou in 1962.
The Notre-Dame Cathedral reopens to the public after previously being damaged by a structural fire in 2019.

Mazan rapes trial: The Judicial Court in Avignon, France, finds Dominique Pelicot guilty of the aggravated rape of his ex-wife Gisèle Pelicot and imposes the maximum sentence of 20 years in prison. The 50 other defendants in the case are also convicted of crimes ranging from attempted rape to aggravated rape, and receive prison sentences ranging from three to 15 years.
A widespread power outage affects Spain and Portugal for hours. Andorra is affected for a few seconds while southern France is lightly affected.
2024–2025 French political crisis: The Bayrou government collapses after losing a no-confidence vote.
The UK, Canada, and Australia announce their formal recognition of Palestine as a sovereign state, with France also doing so the next day.
2025 Louvre heist: Pieces of the French Crown Jewels are stolen during a robbery from the Galerie d'Apollon of the Louvre in Paris.
The Junior Eurovision Song Contest 2025 is held in Tbilisi, Georgia. French contestant Lou Deleuze wins with the song "Ce monde".
France seizes one shadow fleet tanker, under a Russian flag, in the Mediterranean.
The 2026 24 Hours of Le Mans is held in Le Mans, France.

European heatwaves: Wildfires in France, Portugal and Spain force 300,000 people to evacuate their homes. French officials call it the worst wildfire emergency in decades, while officials in Madrid describe it as the worst the region has ever experienced.
Twelve countries, including Canada, France and the United Kingdom, announce plans to introduce or support trade restrictions on goods from Israeli settlements, citing threats to a two-state solution.

2026 French lycée protests: A series of student led protests begin in the outskirts of Paris with students demanding better funding and resources for schools. In early October these protests had spread across France and into neighboring Belgium, with hundreds of thousands taking part and thousands arrested.

2026 French supermarket refrigerator hack: A major cyberattack targets the refrigeration units of hundreds of supermarkets across France, raising the temperature to 50 °C. The hack results in fires and tens of millions of euros worth of losses from food spoilage. Other countries in Europe are also impacted to a lesser extent. It is the first cyberattack to cause major disruption to a nation's food supply chain.
